text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin picks cabinet Members: Martine Aubry named Employment and Solidarity minister, Dominique Strauss-Kahn Economy, Finance and Industry minister, Elisabeth Guigou Justice Minister, Alain Richard Defence minister, Jean-Pierre Chevenement Interior Minister.
-- Air France and railway operator SNCF to be controlled by Communist transport minister who is opposed to SNCF reform and privatisation of airline.
-- CIC may ask for three to four billion francs in shareholder equity from the state if government decides not to go ahead with privatisation, according to chairman Philippe Pontet.
-- Unions to meet with new Industry minister over possible alternative solutions to a planned shutdown of Renault's Belgian Vilvoorde assembly plant.
-- Paris stock exchange not afraid of Communist ministers.
-- Shareholder structure at Havas media group is being reshuffled, 37 percent of the capital changed owner in three months.
-- Credit Lyonnais to launch securitization of some ten billion francs worth of real-estate-related loans.
-- Rexel considering acquisition in Latin America or Asia.
-- CGIP may resort to share buybacks to support share price.
-- French businesses invested some 144 billion francs abroad in 1996, according to a Bank of France report.
-- Privatisation of France Telecom expected to be postponed by the new government.
